B2B vs B2C payments, plus C2B and C2C explained

By the Ibanora teamPublished November 24, 20268 min read

In short

B2B payments go from one business to another, and B2C payments go from a business to a person, such as refunds, payouts and wages. C2B payments go from a person to a business at checkout or for a bill, and C2C payments go between people. Each currency has its own payment systems, such as SEPA for euros; ACH and Fedwire for dollars; Faster Payments, Bacs and CHAPS for pounds; and UAEFTS and Aani for dirhams.

The difference between B2B vs B2C payments is who pays whom. In a B2B payment, one business pays another, for example to settle a supplier invoice. In a B2C payment, a business pays a person: a refund, a marketplace payout or wages. C2B runs the other way, from a person to a business at checkout or when paying a bill. C2C, also called P2P (person to person), is one person paying another, such as money sent to family.

Each currency has its own payment systems, and some schemes are open only to one kind of payer. The sections below show which systems each flow commonly uses. This guide covers euros (EUR), US dollars (USD), British pounds (GBP) and UAE dirhams (AED).

What B2B, B2C, C2B and C2C payments mean

The first letter is the payer and the last letter is the payee. Some payment system operators list typical uses, for example Nacha for the US ACH network, the Federal Reserve, and the Central Bank of the UAE (CBUAE). The other examples below are general illustrations.

FlowWho pays whomEveryday examples
B2B (business to business)A business pays another businessPaying suppliers and vendors
B2C (business to consumer)A business pays a personPayroll by direct deposit, refunds, payouts to sellers
C2B (consumer to business)A person pays a businessOnline checkout, utility bills, loan repayments, subscriptions
C2C or P2P (consumer to consumer)A person pays another personMoney sent to family, splitting a dinner bill, paying a seller for a used item

A marketplace can turn one sale into two flows. When the platform collects the buyer's money and pays the seller later, the buyer makes a C2B payment to the platform and the seller receives a B2C payout from it.

B2B vs B2C payments: the main differences

Some systems are built for large or time-critical payments. The Federal Reserve says its Fedwire Funds Service is generally used for large-value, time-critical payments. In the UK, the Bank of England says companies use CHAPS for high-value and time-sensitive payments, such as paying suppliers or taxes.

A business that receives a B2B payment has to match it to an invoice, so the data sent with the payment matters. A SEPA Credit Transfer lets the payer add up to 140 characters of remittance information for this purpose, according to the European Payments Council (EPC). In the US, Nacha counted 8.08 billion B2B payments on the ACH network in 2025, moving $63.11 trillion.

Businesses can send B2C payouts in bulk. The EPC says SEPA Credit Transfer supports bulk payments, where one debit from the payer's account funds many credits, as in a payroll. The Federal Reserve gives payroll direct deposit and tax refunds as typical ACH credit transfers. In the UAE, the CBUAE runs a separate system for wages, the UAE Wages Protection System (UAEWPS), which it set up in 2009.

C2B and C2C payments: checkout, bills and paying people

A C2B payment can be sent by the customer or collected by the business. With a direct debit, the biller asks for the money with the payer's prior approval, given in a signed mandate (EPC). The UK's Bacs system handled 5.0 billion Direct Debits in 2025, according to Pay.UK, which lists uses such as mobile phone bills, broadband, water and subscriptions. In the US, Nacha counted 17.17 billion consumer ACH payments in 2025, including mortgage, loan and utility payments. The CBUAE introduced the UAE Direct Debit System (UAEDDS) in 2012 for regular payments such as utility bills, insurance, loan repayments and subscriptions.

For payments between people, each of the four currencies has a fast rail:

  • GBP: Pay.UK says the Faster Payment System runs day and night, 365 days a year, for real-time payments of up to £1 million. Pay.UK also points to each bank and building society's own transaction limits.
  • EUR: under the EPC's SCT Inst scheme, the real-time version of SEPA Credit Transfer, the payment providers and the clearing system have nine seconds to make the money available to the payee.
  • USD: the Federal Reserve's FedNow Service went live on July 20, 2023 and lets individuals and businesses send payments through their bank accounts at any time, any day of the year.
  • AED: Al Etihad Payments, a CBUAE subsidiary, launched Aani on October 16, 2023. It runs 24 hours a day, seven days a week, and lets users send money with only the recipient's phone number.

Payment rails and account details for EUR, USD, GBP and AED

Each currency has its own payment systems and its own format for account details. The main ones, as of November 2026:

CurrencyEveryday transfers and debitsReal-time gross settlement (RTGS) or wire systemAccount details for a domestic payment
EURSEPA Credit Transfer, SCT Inst (real-time), SEPA Direct DebitT2, the Eurosystem's real-time gross settlement systemIBAN
USDACH, FedNowFedwire Funds ServiceNine-digit routing number and account number
GBPFaster Payments, BacsCHAPSSort code and account number
AEDAani, UAEDDS for direct debitsUAEFTS, the UAE's real-time gross settlement systemUAE IBAN, 23 characters starting with AE

Euro (EUR): SEPA and T2

The EPC's SEPA schemes for euro credit transfers and direct debits cover the 27 EU member states plus 14 other countries and territories, including the United Kingdom, Switzerland and Norway (EPC). Under the EPC's SEPA Credit Transfer scheme, the rules are the same within one country and between two SEPA countries. The payee receives the full amount, and each customer can only be charged by their own provider.

The SEPA Regulation adds rules that matter for C2B and B2B payments. Providers may not ask customers for the BIC of either bank, so the IBAN is enough. A business that accepts euro credit transfers or collects by direct debit may not insist that the payer's account sits in a particular EU country, as long as the account is reachable. Since the 2024 amendments, the payee's provider must make a real-time euro credit transfer available within 10 seconds, and charges for these transfers may not be higher than for other credit transfers of the same type. The payer's provider must also offer, free of charge, to verify the payee before the payer authorizes a credit transfer. These duties phase in by type of provider and country, with some deadlines in 2027.

Large euro payments between banks settle in T2, the Eurosystem's real-time gross settlement system. The European Central Bank says T2 settles payments one by one in central bank money, with no upper or lower limit on value.

US dollar (USD): ACH, Fedwire and FedNow

The Federal Reserve describes ACH as a nationwide network through which banks send each other batches of electronic credits and debits. Nacha says the network reaches all US bank and credit union accounts, and payments can be processed within hours on the same business day or scheduled one or two business days ahead. As of November 2026, Same Day ACH has a $1 million limit per payment, which Nacha says rises to $10 million on September 17, 2027.

Fedwire Funds Service is a real-time gross settlement system, and the Federal Reserve says its transfers are immediate, final and irrevocable once processed. Both systems identify banks by routing number, listed in the Federal Reserve Banks' E-Payments Routing Directory. Under Regulation CC, an agent of the American Bankers Association assigns each bank its routing number, which has a nine-digit form.

British pound (GBP): Faster Payments, Bacs and CHAPS

Pay.UK says Faster Payments are initiated mainly online, by mobile or by telephone banking. Bacs handles Direct Debits and Direct Credits. CHAPS, run by the Bank of England, settles each payment individually in real time and is mainly used for same-day, high-value payments, including house purchases.

A UK payee gives a sort code and account number. Pay.UK says the sort code is part of the information used to route and settle payments through Bacs, Faster Payments and the Image Clearing System for cheques (Pay.UK). When a customer sets up a new payment, Confirmation of Payee lets the provider check the name, sort code and account number, and returns a match, a close match, no match, or unavailable.

UAE dirham (AED): UAEFTS, Aani and the UAE IBAN

The UAE Funds Transfer System (UAEFTS) is the country's real-time gross settlement system, owned and run by the CBUAE and operating since 2001. Banks and other financial institutions move funds through their accounts at the central bank, and each transfer settles on its own without netting.

The CBUAE says a UAE IBAN is always 23 characters: the country code AE, two check digits, a three-digit bank identifier and a 16-digit account number. Customers must use an IBAN for both domestic and international electronic payments, and transfers to UAE payees without a valid IBAN may face extra rejection charges.

How cross-border B2B payments and other flows work

For cross-border bank payments, Swift provides the messaging network. Swift says it does not move money itself: banks send payment instructions over its network, and the funds move through banks, fintechs and other institutions.

A cross-border payment can pass through intermediary banks. As of November 2026, Swift says 86% of payments on its network go directly or through a single intermediary, and 90% of cross-border payments reach the beneficiary's bank in under an hour. Swift adds that delays often happen in the last step, between the payee's bank receiving the money and crediting the customer's account.

The IBAN is an international account number format designed to automate cross-border payments. It follows the ISO 13616 standard, and Swift is the registration authority that publishes the IBAN Registry of national formats. Where a country has no IBAN, the CBUAE says payers still need the bank's BIC (also called a SWIFT code) together with the domestic account number. In the US, Nacha's International ACH Transaction (IAT) format marks ACH payments that cross borders and carries information on all parties.

A change of currency adds one more step: someone converts the money, and the rate they use is part of the cost. As an example, on a $1,000 invoice paid in euros, an exchange rate 1% worse than the mid-market rate costs $10, before any transfer fee. The same arithmetic applies to a refund on a foreign purchase or money sent to family abroad. For how accounts that hold several currencies work, see what a multi-currency account is.

What to check before you pay in another currency

  • The account details in the right format for the currency: an IBAN for EUR and AED, a routing and account number for USD, a sort code and account number for GBP.
  • The payee's name. In the UK, Pay.UK says more than 140 payment providers offer Confirmation of Payee. For euro credit transfers, the SEPA Regulation requires the payer's provider to offer verification of the payee, with providers in EU countries that do not use the euro given until July 9, 2027.
  • Which currency the receiving account holds, and who converts.
  • Limits for large B2B payments, such as the £1 million Faster Payments limit and the $1 million Same Day ACH limit, as of November 2026.
  • Every fee and the exchange rate, from your own provider, before you send.

Questions

Is P2P the same as C2C?

Yes. Both describe a payment from one person to another. Nacha lists paying a friend for dinner among consumer ACH payments, and the CBUAE says Aani lets users send money in the UAE with only the recipient's phone number.

Can a business make both B2B and B2C payments?

Yes. A flow is named by who pays whom, so one company can send B2B payments to its suppliers and B2C payments, such as refunds, to its customers. Some rules change with the payer: in SEPA, the EPC runs SDD Core for consumers and a separate SDD B2B scheme for business payers.

How long do B2B payments take?

It depends on the rail. Nacha says ACH payments can be processed within hours on the same business day or be scheduled one or two business days ahead, while Fedwire transfers are immediate and final once processed. Real-time euro credit transfers under SCT Inst must reach the payee within 10 seconds, and as of November 2026 Swift says 90% of cross-border payments reach the beneficiary bank in under an hour.

Do you need an IBAN to pay someone in the UAE?

Yes, for electronic payments. The CBUAE says customers must use an IBAN for domestic and international electronic payments, and a UAE IBAN has 23 characters starting with AE. Transfers to UAE payees without a valid IBAN may face extra rejection charges.
